definitions.explanation: A liquid secreted by organs in the digestive system that breaks down food. Includes gastric juice, bile, pancreatic juice, and intestinal fluids.

examples.japanese: {胃|い}は{消化液|しょうかえき}を{分泌|ぶんぴつ}する。
{消化液|しょうかえき}が{食|た}べ{物|もの}を{分解|ぶんかい}する。
ストレスで{消化液|しょうかえき}の{分泌|ぶんぴつ}が{減|へ}ると、{消化不良|しょうかふりょう}になることがある。
examples.english: When the secretion of digestive fluids decreases due to stress, it can lead to indigestion.

notes:
Compound of {消化|しょうか} (digestion) + {液|えき} (liquid/fluid). A standard biology and health term. The {液|えき} suffix is used for many bodily and chemical fluids: {血液|けつえき} (blood), {唾液|だえき} (saliva), {体液|たいえき} (body fluid).

The main types of {消化液|しょうかえき}:
- {胃液|いえき}: gastric juice
- {胆汁|たんじゅう}: bile
- {膵液|すいえき}: pancreatic juice
- {腸液|ちょうえき}: intestinal fluid

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {消化液|しょうかえき}の{分泌|ぶんぴつ}: secretion of digestive fluids
- {消化液|しょうかえき}が{出|で}る: digestive fluids come out
- {消化液|しょうかえき}で{溶|と}かす: to dissolve with digestive fluid

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {胃液|いえき}: gastric juice — specifically the digestive fluid in the stomach
- {消化酵素|しょうかこうそ}: digestive enzyme — the active chemical component within digestive fluids
- {唾液|だえき}: saliva — also contains digestive enzymes, but primarily associated with the mouth
